review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

11:1.sourceText: μιμηταί μου γίνεσθε, καθὼς κἀγὼ Χριστοῦ.
11:1.targetText: You are to imitate me, just as I imitate Christ.

groups.note: μιμηταί ("imitators") is rendered as the verb imitate, and BSB repeats it after I.
The imperative γίνεσθε ("become") is rendered You are to.
κἀγώ ("I also") is rendered I.

11:2.sourceText: Ἐπαινῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς ὅτι πάντα μου μέμνησθε καὶ καθὼς παρέδωκα ὑμῖν τὰς παραδόσεις κατέχετε.
11:2.targetText: Now I commend you for remembering me in everything and for maintaining the traditions, just as I passed them on to you.

groups.note: ὅτι ("because") governs both verbs; BSB repeats for.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for passed on; the Greek has none.

11:3.sourceText: Θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς εἰδέναι ὅτι παντὸς ἀνδρὸς ἡ κεφαλὴ ὁ Χριστός ἐστιν, κεφαλὴ δὲ γυναικὸς ὁ ἀνήρ, κεφαλὴ δὲ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὁ Θεός.
11:3.targetText: But I want you to understand that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is man, and the head of Christ is God.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula; the Greek clause has no verb.
English supplies a copula; the Greek clause has no verb.

11:4.sourceText: πᾶς ἀνὴρ προσευχόμενος ἢ προφητεύων κατὰ κεφαλῆς ἔχων καταισχύνει τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ.
11:4.targetText: Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors his head.

groups.note: κατὰ κεφαλῆς ἔχων ("having down over the head") is rendered with his head covered.
The participle ἔχων ("having") is rendered with.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the possessive; the Greek has no pronoun here.

11:5.sourceText: πᾶσα δὲ γυνὴ προσευχομένη ἢ προφητεύουσα ἀκατακαλύπτῳ τῇ κεφαλῇ καταισχύνει τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτῆς· ἓν γάρ ἐστιν καὶ τὸ αὐτὸ τῇ ἐξυρημένῃ.
11:5.targetText: And every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head, for it is just as if her head were shaved.

groups.note: The article τῇ is used as a possessive ("her").
The dative ἀκατακαλύπτῳ τῇ κεφαλῇ ("with uncovered head") supplies with.
ἓν … καὶ τὸ αὐτό ("one and the same") is rendered just as if.
τῇ ἐξυρημένῃ ("the shaved woman") is rendered her head were shaved.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:6.sourceText: εἰ γὰρ οὐ κατακαλύπτεται γυνή, καὶ κειράσθω· εἰ δὲ αἰσχρὸν γυναικὶ τὸ κείρασθαι ἢ ξυρᾶσθαι, κατακαλυπτέσθω.
11:6.targetText: If a woman does not cover her head, she should have her hair cut off. And if it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut or shaved off, she should cover her head.

groups.note: The middle κατακαλύπτεται ("veils herself") is rendered cover her head.

targetPhrases.text: she should have her hair cut off

groups.note: The imperative κειράσθω ("let her be shorn") is rendered she should have her hair cut off.
The article τό makes the infinitives a noun phrase; it joins κείρασθαι.
The imperative κατακαλυπτέσθω ("let her veil herself") is rendered she should cover her head.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.
BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject and copula; the Greek clause has no verb.

11:7.sourceText: ἀνὴρ μὲν γὰρ οὐκ ὀφείλει κατακαλύπτεσθαι τὴν κεφαλήν, εἰκὼν καὶ δόξα Θεοῦ ὑπάρχων· ἡ γυνὴ δὲ δόξα ἀνδρός ἐστιν.
11:7.targetText: A man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but the woman is the glory of man.

groups.note: The article τήν is used as a possessive ("his").
The participle ὑπάρχων ("being") is rendered since … is.

unmappedSource.reason: μέν marks the first side of the contrast and has no English word.
BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: A participle has no person; English supplies the subject.

11:8.sourceText: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἀνὴρ ἐκ γυναικός, ἀλλὰ γυνὴ ἐξ ἀνδρός·
11:8.targetText: For man did not come from woman, but woman from man.

groups.note: ἐστιν … ἐκ ("is from") is rendered did come from.

11:9.sourceText: καὶ γὰρ οὐκ ἐκτίσθη ἀνὴρ διὰ τὴν γυναῖκα, ἀλλὰ γυνὴ διὰ τὸν ἄνδρα.
11:9.targetText: Neither was man created for woman, but woman for man.

groups.note: καί … οὐκ ("and … not") is rendered Neither.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:10.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτο ὀφείλει ἡ γυνὴ ἐξουσίαν ἔχειν ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς διὰ τοὺς ἀγγέλους.
11:10.targetText: For this reason a woman ought to have a sign of authority on her head, because of the angels.

groups.note: The article τῆς is used as a possessive ("her").

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a sign of; the Greek has only ἐξουσίαν ("authority").

11:11.sourceText: πλὴν οὔτε γυνὴ χωρὶς ἀνδρὸς οὔτε ἀνὴρ χωρὶς γυναικὸς ἐν Κυρίῳ·
11:11.targetText: In the Lord, however, woman is not independent of man, nor is man independent of woman.

groups.note: χωρίς ("apart from") is rendered independent of.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula; the Greek clause has no verb.
English supplies a copula; the Greek clause has no verb.

11:12.sourceText: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἡ γυνὴ ἐκ τοῦ ἀνδρός, οὕτως καὶ ὁ ἀνὴρ διὰ τῆς γυναικός· τὰ δὲ πάντα ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ.
11:12.targetText: For just as woman came from man, so also man is born of woman. But everything comes from God.

groups.note: διά ("through") is rendered of after the supplied is born.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb; the Greek clause has none.
English supplies a verb; the Greek clause has only διά ("through").
English supplies a verb; the Greek clause has none.

11:13.sourceText: ἐν ὑμῖν αὐτοῖς κρίνατε· πρέπον ἐστὶν γυναῖκα ἀκατακάλυπτον τῷ Θεῷ προσεύχεσθαι;
11:13.targetText: Judge for yourselves: Is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?

groups.note: ἐν ὑμῖν αὐτοῖς ("among yourselves") is rendered for yourselves.
ἀκατακάλυπτον ("unveiled") describes the woman; BSB renders it with her head uncovered.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:14.sourceText: οὐδὲ ἡ φύσις αὐτὴ διδάσκει ὑμᾶς ὅτι ἀνὴρ μὲν ἐὰν κομᾷ, ἀτιμία αὐτῷ ἐστιν,
11:14.targetText: Doesn’t nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a disgrace to him,

groups.note: οὐδέ ("not even") is rendered Doesn’t.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the particle μέν untranslated.

11:15.sourceText: γυνὴ δὲ ἐὰν κομᾷ, δόξα αὐτῇ ἐστιν; ὅτι ἡ κόμη ἀντὶ περιβολαίου δέδοται αὐτῇ.
11:15.targetText: but that if a woman has long hair, it is her glory? For long hair is given to her as a covering.

groups.note: ἀντί ("in place of") is rendered as.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English repeats that from v. 14, where ὅτι introduces both clauses.

11:16.sourceText: Εἰ δέ τις δοκεῖ φιλόνεικος εἶναι, ἡμεῖς τοιαύτην συνήθειαν οὐκ ἔχομεν, οὐδὲ αἱ ἐκκλησίαι τοῦ Θεοῦ.
11:16.targetText: If anyone is inclined to dispute this, we have no other practice, nor do the churches of God.

groups.note: δοκεῖ ("seems, thinks") is rendered is inclined.
φιλόνεικος εἶναι ("to be contentious") is rendered to dispute.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
BSB’s other does not render τοιαύτην ("such"), so it has no English word here.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for dispute.
English says no other practice; the Greek has τοιαύτην ("such").
English supplies do for the verb have understood in this clause.

11:17.sourceText: Τοῦτο δὲ παραγγέλλων οὐκ ἐπαινῶ ὅτι οὐκ εἰς τὸ κρεῖσσον ἀλλὰ εἰς τὸ ἧσσον συνέρχεσθε.
11:17.targetText: In the following instructions I have no praise to offer, because your gatherings do more harm than good.

groups.note: τοῦτο ("this") points to the instructions that follow.
The participle παραγγέλλων ("instructing") is rendered In … instructions.
ἐπαινῶ ("I praise") is rendered I have … praise to offer.
οὐκ … ἀλλά ("not … but") is recast as the comparison more … than.
εἰς τὸ κρεῖσσον ("for the better") is rendered good.
εἰς τὸ ἧσσον ("for the worse") is rendered more harm.
συνέρχεσθε ("you come together") is rendered your gatherings.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb; gatherings renders the Greek verb συνέρχεσθε.

11:18.sourceText: πρῶτον μὲν γὰρ συνερχομένων ὑμῶν ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ ἀκούω σχίσματα ἐν ὑμῖν ὑπάρχειν, καὶ μέρος τι πιστεύω.
11:18.targetText: First of all, I hear that when you come together as a church, there are divisions among you, and in part I believe it.

groups.note: The genitive absolute συνερχομένων ὑμῶν ("you coming together") is rendered when you come together.
ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ ("in assembly") is rendered as a church.
μέρος τι ("some part") is rendered in part.

unmappedSource.reason: μέν marks the first point and has no English word.
BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds that to introduce the content clause.
English supplies an object for believe.

11:19.sourceText: δεῖ γὰρ καὶ αἱρέσεις ἐν ὑμῖν εἶναι, ἵνα καὶ οἱ δόκιμοι φανεροὶ γένωνται ἐν ὑμῖν.
11:19.targetText: And indeed, there must be differences among you to show which of you are approved.

groups.note: γάρ ("for") is rendered indeed.
The article οἱ ("the ones") with δόκιμοι is rendered which.
φανεροὶ γένωνται ("may become evident") is rendered show.
ἐν ὑμῖν ("among you") is rendered of you.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula.

11:20.sourceText: Συνερχομένων οὖν ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ οὐκ ἔστιν κυριακὸν δεῖπνον φαγεῖν·
11:20.targetText: Now then, when you come together, it is not the Lord’s Supper you eat.

groups.note: The genitive absolute συνερχομένων ὑμῶν ("you coming together") is rendered when you come together.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB has no separate word for ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό ("in the same place"); come together covers it.

unmappedTarget.reason: An infinitive has no person; English supplies you.

11:21.sourceText: ἕκαστος γὰρ τὸ ἴδιον δεῖπνον προλαμβάνει ἐν τῷ φαγεῖν, καὶ ὃς μὲν πεινᾷ, ὃς δὲ μεθύει.
11:21.targetText: For as you eat, each of you goes ahead without sharing his meal. While one remains hungry, another gets drunk.

groups.note: ἴδιον ("own") is rendered his.
προλαμβάνει ("takes beforehand") is rendered goes ahead without sharing.
ἐν τῷ with the infinitive is a temporal "as".
μέν … δέ ("on the one hand … on the other") marks the contrast, rendered While.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence and leaves καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: An infinitive has no person; English supplies you.
English adds of you to specify the group.

11:22.sourceText: μὴ γὰρ οἰκίας οὐκ ἔχετε εἰς τὸ ἐσθίειν καὶ πίνειν; ἢ τῆς ἐκκλησίας τοῦ Θεοῦ καταφρονεῖτε, καὶ καταισχύνετε τοὺς μὴ ἔχοντας; τί εἴπω ὑμῖν; ἐπαινέσω ὑμᾶς; ἐν τούτῳ οὐκ ἐπαινῶ.
11:22.targetText: Don’t you have your own homes in which to eat and drink? Or do you despise the church of God and humiliate those who have nothing? What can I say to you? Shall I praise you for this? No, I will not!

groups.note: εἰς τό with the infinitives ("for eating") is rendered in which to.
The article τούς with the participle ἔχοντας forms those who have.
μή ("not") with have is rendered nothing.
ἐν τούτῳ ("in this") is rendered for this.
ἐπαινῶ ("I praise") is rendered I will, with praise understood.

unmappedSource.reason: μή marks a question expecting the answer no; BSB has no separate word for it.
BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds your own; the Greek has only οἰκίας ("houses").
English adds No to answer the question.

11:23.sourceText: ἐγὼ γὰρ παρέλαβον ἀπὸ τοῦ Κυρίου, ὃ καὶ παρέδωκα ὑμῖν, ὅτι ὁ Κύριος Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῇ νυκτὶ ᾗ παρεδίδετο ἔλαβεν ἄρτον
11:23.targetText: For I received from the Lord what I also passed on to you: The Lord Jesus, on the night He was betrayed, took bread,

unmappedSource.reason: BSB marks ὅτι ("that") with a colon.
BSB leaves the relative ᾗ ("in which") unexpressed in the night He was betrayed.

11:24.sourceText: καὶ εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ εἶπεν Τοῦτό μού ἐστιν τὸ σῶμα τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν· τοῦτο ποιεῖτε εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν.
11:24.targetText: and when He had given thanks, He broke it and said, “This is My body, which is for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”

groups.note: The article τό, which makes ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν describe the body, is rendered which.
The possessive ἐμήν ("my") is rendered of Me.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for broke; the Greek has none.
English supplies a copula.
A participle has no person; English supplies the subject.

11:25.sourceText: ὡσαύτως καὶ τὸ ποτήριον μετὰ τὸ δειπνῆσαι, λέγων Τοῦτο τὸ ποτήριον ἡ καινὴ διαθήκη ἐστὶν ἐν τῷ ἐμῷ αἵματι· τοῦτο ποιεῖτε, ὁσάκις ἐὰν πίνητε, εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν.
11:25.targetText: In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood; do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me.”

groups.note: The articular infinitive τὸ δειπνῆσαι ("the dining") is rendered supper.
ὁσάκις ἐάν ("as often as") works as one unit.
The possessive ἐμήν ("my") is rendered of Me.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated after In the same way.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the verb; the Greek carries over ἔλαβεν from v. 23.
English supplies an object for drink; the Greek has none.

11:26.sourceText: ὁσάκις γὰρ ἐὰν ἐσθίητε τὸν ἄρτον τοῦτον καὶ τὸ ποτήριον πίνητε, τὸν θάνατον τοῦ Κυρίου καταγγέλλετε, ἄχρι οὗ ἔλθῃ.
11:26.targetText: For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes.

groups.note: ὁσάκις ἐάν ("as often as") works as one unit.
The article τό is rendered this, matching this bread.
ἄχρι οὗ is one conjunction, until.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:27.sourceText: ὥστε ὃς ἂν ἐσθίῃ τὸν ἄρτον ἢ πίνῃ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦ Κυρίου ἀναξίως, ἔνοχος ἔσται τοῦ σώματος καὶ τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ Κυρίου.
11:27.targetText: Therefore, whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be guilty of sinning against the body and blood of the Lord.

groups.note: ὃς ἄν ("whoever") works as one unit.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies sinning against; the Greek has ἔνοχος ("guilty, liable") with the genitive.

11:28.sourceText: δοκιμαζέτω δὲ ἄνθρωπος ἑαυτόν, καὶ οὕτως ἐκ τοῦ ἄρτου ἐσθιέτω καὶ ἐκ τοῦ ποτηρίου πινέτω·
11:28.targetText: Each one must examine himself before he eats of the bread and drinks of the cup.

groups.note: The imperative δοκιμαζέτω ("let him examine") is rendered must examine.
ἄνθρωπος ("a person") is rendered Each one.
καὶ οὕτως ("and so") is rendered before: the eating follows the examining.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.

11:29.sourceText: ὁ γὰρ ἐσθίων καὶ πίνων κρίμα ἑαυτῷ ἐσθίει καὶ πίνει μὴ διακρίνων τὸ σῶμα.
11:29.targetText: For anyone who eats and drinks without recognizing the body eats and drinks judgment on himself.

groups.note: The article governs both participles: "the one eating … and drinking".

11:30.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτο ἐν ὑμῖν πολλοὶ ἀσθενεῖς καὶ ἄρρωστοι καὶ κοιμῶνται ἱκανοί.
11:30.targetText: That is why many among you are weak and sick, and a number of you have fallen asleep.

groups.note: διὰ τοῦτο ("because of this") is rendered That is why.
ἱκανοί ("a good many") is rendered a number.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula.
English adds of you to specify the group.

11:31.sourceText: εἰ δὲ ἑαυτοὺς διεκρίνομεν, οὐκ ἂν ἐκρινόμεθα·
11:31.targetText: Now if we judged ourselves properly, we would not come under judgment.

groups.note: διεκρίνομεν ("we discerned") is rendered judged … properly.
ἄν with the imperfect marks the unreal result, would.
The passive ἐκρινόμεθα ("we were being judged") is rendered come under judgment.

11:32.sourceText: κρινόμενοι δὲ ὑπὸ τοῦ Κυρίου παιδευόμεθα, ἵνα μὴ σὺν τῷ κόσμῳ κατακριθῶμεν.
11:32.targetText: But when we are judged by the Lord, we are being disciplined so that we will not be condemned with the world.

unmappedTarget.reason: A participle has no person; English supplies we.

11:33.sourceText: ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου, συνερχόμενοι εἰς τὸ φαγεῖν ἀλλήλους ἐκδέχεσθε.
11:33.targetText: So, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.

groups.note: εἰς τό with the infinitive is rendered to.

unmappedTarget.reason: A participle has no person; English supplies you.

11:34.sourceText: εἴ τις πεινᾷ, ἐν οἴκῳ ἐσθιέτω, ἵνα μὴ εἰς κρίμα συνέρχησθε. Τὰ δὲ λοιπὰ ὡς ἂν ἔλθω διατάξομαι.
11:34.targetText: If anyone is hungry, he should eat at home, so that when you come together it will not result in judgment. And when I come, I will give instructions about the remaining matters.

groups.note: εἰς κρίμα ("for judgment") is rendered result in judgment.
ὡς ἄν ("whenever") is rendered when.

unmappedTarget.reason: English recasts the purpose clause with when; the Greek has no word for it.
English supplies a subject and auxiliary for the recast clause.
